title: Ridged rib pram blanket
subtitle: A small pram blanket with alternating garter and purl-ridge bands.
excerpt: A 60 by 80 cm pram blanket in DK worked flat as a single panel. Alternating bands of four knit rows and four purl rows from the public side produce a deep-ridged reversible fabric that is more elastic than plain garter stitch, fitting snugly over a pram blanket clip.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 6th series (1890), §Pram Wraps, describes ridged patterns made by alternating knit and purl rows as a standard pram cover stitch, valued for the way the ridges grip pram edges and clips.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 40 rows = 10 × 10 cm in ridge rib on 4 mm needles, unblocked.
knitting.gaugeInPatternStitch: 22 sts × 40 rows = 10 × 10 cm over the ridge-rib pattern (alternating 4-row garter and 4-row purl bands).

glossaryTerms.definition: A stitch pattern formed by alternating bands of knit rows and purl rows. When worked flat, four rows of knitting followed by four rows of purling (from the right side) produces deep horizontal ridges that give the fabric elasticity and a reversible appearance.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat in a
ridge-rib pattern
on 4 mm needles, finishing at 60 cm wide by 80 cm long.

Single-panel construction produces a blanket with no seams, which is easier to manage in a pram. The ridge-rib stitch, made by alternating blocks of four knit rows and four purl rows, was chosen over plain garter because it lies flat on both faces like garter but with a more elastic, deeper-ridged fabric that grips pram blanket clips better than plain garter. Budget about 160 g (about 350 m / 380 yards) of machine-washable DK. Buy all the yarn at once: this blanket is small enough to use from a single large skein. Fits a standard pram and folds compact for a changing bag.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 160 g (about 350 m / 380 yards) of DK-weight machine-washable yarn
items.substitutions: Superwash merino DK or DK wool-cotton blend. Cotton DK works but is heavier and less elastic.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) straight or circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 40 rows to 10 cm over ridge rib on 4 mm needles, unblocked. Ridge rib sits slightly shorter per row than plain garter stitch because the purl rows pull in. Work a 15 cm swatch in the full pattern to get an accurate row gauge for this blanket.
If your row gauge is 38 rows per 10 cm instead of 40, the blanket will be about 84 cm long at 320 rows rather than 80 cm. Measure the blanket by tape rather than by row count.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 132 stitches. Long-tail tail: (4 × 132) / 10 + 15 = 52.8 + 15 = 68 cm. Measure 80 cm of tail.
Body
Rows 1 to 4 (RS rows 1 and 3, WS rows 2 and 4): knit every stitch on every row.
Rows 5 to 8 (RS rows 5 and 7, WS rows 6 and 8): purl every stitch on every row.
Repeat this 8-row sequence until the blanket measures 80 cm from the cast-on edge. The ridges form where the knit and purl bands meet.
When you set this aside between sessions, note which band you are in (knit or purl) and which row within the band.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 160 (about 40 cm): count across. You should have 132 stitches. At row 318 (about 79.5 cm): count again before the final cast-off row.
Common faults
Working knit rows instead of purl rows in the purl band: the band appears as garter (knit both sides) rather than a distinct purl ridge. Track the band number on a sticky note or use a row counter.

Purl rows tighter than knit rows: many knitters purl more tightly. If the blanket shows alternating bands of different tension widths, work the purl rows on a needle one size larger or consciously loosen the purl tension.
Cast-off
Cast off knitwise across all stitches with a relaxed tension. End the blanket at the last row of a complete 8-row repeat if possible so the two edges match visually.
Finishing
Weave in the two ends on the wrong side, running each tail at least 5 cm along a ridge. Trim. The ridge-rib pattern is reversible: either face can be the public side.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle if the yarn label permits. Lay flat to dry. The ridge pattern recovers its elasticity after washing and drying flat.
What to try next

From ridge rib, a two-colour version is straightforward: work each 4-row band in a different colour, carrying the unused yarn up the edge as for a striped blanket. The stitch pattern and cast-on are the same; only the colour switch at every band changes the technique.
